title: L'Imperativo Informale
subtitle: Giving commands and instructions with tu, noi, voi.
objectives: Form the informal imperative for tu, noi, voi
Form the negative tu imperative correctly
Attach object and reflexive pronouns to the informal imperative

content.intro: The informal imperative is how you give instructions, make suggestions, or issue commands to someone you'd address with tu — a friend, a child, someone your own age.
content.explanation: The tu and voi imperative forms match the present tense exactly for -ere and -ire verbs, but -are verbs change their tu ending from -i to -a. The noi form ("let's...") is identical to the noi present tense in every conjugation. The negative tu form is special: non + infinitive, not the expected non + imperative.

rules.heading: a) Negative tu — non + infinitive
rules.body: Non parlare! (Don't speak!) — not "non parla". Noi and voi simply add non before the normal form: Non parliamo. Non parlate.

rules.heading: b) Pronouns attach to the end
rules.body: Aiutami! (Help me!) Chiamalo! (Call him!) Alzati! (Get up! — reflexive) In the negative, they can attach to the infinitive instead: Non aiutarmi! / Non mi aiutare!

rules.heading: c) Irregular tu imperatives
rules.body: andare → va'/vai, dare → da'/dai, fare → fa'/fai, stare → sta'/stai, dire → di' — short, apostrophized forms, both versions correct.

examples.en: Let's go to the movies tonight!

examples.it: Non ti preoccupare, andrà tutto bene.
examples.en: Don't worry, everything will be fine.

commonMistakes.why: The negative tu imperative uses non + infinitive, not the affirmative imperative form with non added.
Pronouns attach to the end of the informal imperative form, not before it as with a conjugated verb.
Voi is plural — addressing a single friend needs the tu form, parla.

items.explanation: -are verbs change the tu ending to -a in the imperative.
Voi imperative of fare matches its present tense: fate.
Pronouns attach directly to the end of the imperative verb.
Negative tu imperative needs the infinitive, not the present tense form.

summary: Tu imperative: -are verbs use -a; -ere/-ire verbs match the present tense tu form.
Negative tu imperative is always non + infinitive — a genuine exception, not the affirmative + non.
Object and reflexive pronouns attach to the end of the imperative verb (Aiutami!, Alzati!).
